title: The Bright Signal
premise: Emrys Okafor, a terraformer on the colony world Verdance, has spent fifteen years quietly tending a garden for future generations while hauling cargo through orbits patrolled by the Meridian Combine. When the colony's children begin sharing an identical dream of a burning ship, Emrys recognizes it as the Aurelia, a refugee vessel destroyed fifteen years ago—an event erased from every official record, and one he survived in secret. As the children's dream spreads and the Combine moves to silence 'dream-talk,' Emrys must choose between his lifelong invisibility and testifying to what he saw, piecing together physical evidence from the wreck site before the jump window to Earth closes with the truth sealed inside it. In the end, he broadcasts the recovered black-box memory during the window's final minutes; the Combine's records crack, the colonists claim their own history, and Emrys plants the last of the garden's seedlings—no longer for people not yet born, but for people finally willing to remember.
about_author: Felix Thackeray is the pen name of a former hydrologist who spent six years working remote research stations before turning to fiction. They write quiet, character-driven science fiction about ordinary people caught inside enormous machinery.

chapters.title: Seedlings Under a Borrowed Sky
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A day in his routine: tending the terraform garden, hauling cargo past Combine patrol buoys, keeping his head down as he has for fifteen years. We learn he never talks about his arrival on Verdance. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as contentment—the reader senses a locked door in him.

chapters.title: The Dream That Belonged to Everyone
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Nia Adeyemi, age nine, daughter of a fellow terraformer. She wakes screaming from a dream of a burning ship and finds seven other children dreamed the same thing, down to the hull number. Adults dismiss it as a shared nightmare. Emotional beat: uncanny dread, and the first crack in the colony's calm.

chapters.title: Hull Number 7741
chapters.summary: Emrys hears Nia recite the dream at the communal hall and freezes: she describes the Aurelia, the refugee ship he watched burn in orbit fifteen years ago—a ship that officially never existed. He says nothing, but begins checking old manifests. Emotional beat: terror of recognition; the past knocking on a door he welded shut.

chapters.title: Records Like Fresh Snow
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. He digs through archives and finds the Aurelia scrubbed from every log—passenger lists, flight plans, even the crater where debris supposedly fell is marked as a meteor strike. The Combine administrator, Voss, notices his queries. Emotional beat: gaslit vertigo; the horror of a world whose paperwork contradicts his own eyes.

chapters.title: What the Children Keep Seeing
chapters.summary: Nia's POV. The dream evolves: now the children see faces at the portholes, and one face recurs—a man holding a child. Nia sketches him; it looks like a younger Emrys. The children begin meeting secretly to compare dreams. Emotional beat: eerie solidarity among the young, and Emrys cornered by innocence.

chapters.title: Voss Offers a Quiet Life
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Administrator Voss privately confronts him: she knows who he is, offers him a promotion and passage on the next jump window if he stops asking questions—and hints the children spreading 'contagious fictions' will be sent Earthside for evaluation. Emotional beat: temptation and threat braided together; loyalty to the colony versus self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Wreck Beneath the Ice
chapters.summary: Emrys, Nia's mother Sefu, and two trusted haulers fly to the meteor 'crater' under cover of a cargo run. Beneath the ice: fused alloy matching no asteroid, and a scorched escape pod—with a black-box memory core still intact. Emotional beat: grief made physical; touching the wreckage he fled from at last.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV, interwoven with flashback. We finally learn the full truth: he was the Aurelia's junior engineer, escaped in the pod while the Combine fired on the ship carrying refugees the colony's founders had promised to take in, then accepted silence in exchange for a new identity. Emotional beat: shame and confession—he must admit his survival was bought with complicity.

chapters.title: Jump Window
chapters.summary: Climax. The Combine seals the archive, detains the dream-talking children, and prepares the jump window departure that will carry the evidence away forever—or carry Emrys to safety. Emrys hijacks his own cargo hauler's broadcast array, uploading the black-box memory to every colony screen as Voss's security closes in. Emotional beat: desperate, blazing defiance; loyalty to truth over loyalty to his own skin.

chapters.title: The Garden Remembers
chapters.summary: Resolution. The broadcast shows the massacre plainly; the colonists refuse to load the jump freighter until the children are released and an independent inquiry is opened, stranding Voss's authority. The dream stops—the children say it 'finished.' Emrys plants the final seedlings with Nia beside him, no longer invisible. Emotional beat: belonging earned through truth; mourning and hope sharing one row of soil.
